title: KV stability locks and distribution-aware profiling for long-context models
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: provide a reproducible workflow for generating and publishing KV cache performance profiles per model that are sensitive to sequence-length distribution, and introduce a deterministic 'stability lock' (version pin) lifecycle that minimizes regression risk for long-context customers. This ticket covers data collection, profile aggregation, pin lifecycle rules, and the publishing pipeline into the model catalog for use by routing/serving and rollout logic.

Why this matters: long-context workloads expose different KV access patterns and memory pressure; naive pinning of a single 'best' variant can regress latency or OOM on heavy-tail sequence distributions. We need a distribution-aware profile that surfaces per-bucket metrics (latency, p95/p99, memory, kv-hit-rate) and a locking mechanism that keeps a model variant pinned while automated stability checks pass.

Scope:
- Design sequence-length bucket schema and sampling strategy for production traffic (online + offline batch).
- Implement a lightweight collector that enriches existing request traces with KV metadata (kv-size, kv-evictions, prefix-hit-rate) and sequence-length bucket.
- Aggregation job that converts samples into published profile artifacts (flat JSON lines with histogram summaries).
- Introduce 'stability lock' API: create / renew / expire pins with metadata (reason, profile-id, expiry, owner).
- Integration in model-catalog: link profiles to pinned versions and surface warnings when profile metrics cross thresholds.
- Console dashboard widgets showing per-model sequence distribution, p99 by bucket, and active locks.

Non-goals: changing the runtime kernel selection logic in this ticket (we will expose profiles for runtime teams to consume in follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Sequence-length bucket schema defined and documented in Confluence (buckets: 1-64, 65-256, 257-1024, 1025-4096, >4096) and agreed with runtime team
Collector deployed to canary (10% of traffic) and producing KV-enriched traces to telemetry cluster
Aggregation job runs daily and produces profile artifacts in model-catalog with per-bucket metrics (avg latency, p95, p99, kv-memory, kv-hit-rate)
Stability lock API implemented and validated: create, renew, list, expire; locks are immutable once created except for renew/expire actions
Pin lifecycle policy enforced: auto-expire after configured ttl (default 30 days) and automatic revalidation job that marks locks 'stale' if p99 regresses >15% vs baseline
Console shows profile and lock state; customers can view which variant is pinned and reason field
End-to-end test coverage for collector -> aggregator -> catalog publishing, and an integration test that simulates a heavy-tail sequence distribution

implementation_notes: Collector: extend existing request enrichers, add sequence-length bucketing at ingestion time to avoid re-processing raw traces
Sampling policy: 1% uniform sampling + adaptive spike sampling for requests > 2048 tokens and all OOM/traceback events

Aggregation: summary artifacts are compressed newline-delimited JSON; each artifact contains model_id, variant_id, profile_id, bucket, samples, avg_latency_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, median_kv_bytes, kv_eviction_rate, kv_hit_rate
Storage: publish artifacts to model-catalog S3 prefix: s3://model-catalog/kv-profiles/{model_id}/{profile_id}.jsonl and register metadata via catalog API
Lock API: store locks in existing catalog DB table 'model_locks' with fields: lock_id, model_id, variant_id, profile_id, owner, reason, created_at, expires_at, status
Auto-validation job: nightly job that compares latest profile to pinned baseline and updates lock state to 'stale' when p99 regresses >15% or kv_eviction_rate increases >10pp
Rollout impact: when a lock is present, routing should prefer the pinned variant until lock expires; falls back to policy-driven selection if pinned variant is unhealthy
Observability: create per-model alert rules for p99 delta and kv_eviction spikes; integrate with incident runbooks
Backward compatibility: runtime will ignore missing profile artifacts; catalog should surface 'no-profile' state rather than failing requests
